messages:
oliver: Heads up — GHAS scanner workers started spamming retries this morning after KMS failures, causing queue backpressure and some files to be rescanned multiple times. Noticing a spike in duplicate SNYK/Trivy runs.
emily: ugh — any logs? is this the decrypt error we've been seeing? :grimacing:
oliver: logs show KMS decrypt errors followed by our scanner retry loop. snippet:```\n2024-06-01T09:12:03Z scanner-worker-12 ERROR decrypt: kms.Decrypt failed: AccessDenied\n2024-06-01T09:12:03Z scanner-worker-12 INFO retrying scan for repo: redwood/app-frontend attempt=1\n2024-06-01T09:12:04Z scanner-worker-12 INFO started trivy scan job id=xyz\n```\nraj: that looks like the KMS key policy dropped the scanner role after last week's RBAC cleanup. I pushed a revert to infra-iam a few hours ago to narrow the blast radius, but maybe some machines still have cached creds.
maria: can we short-circuit retries for decrypt errors? if KMS returns AccessDenied, retries will only make it worse and flood GHAS webhooks. would prefer a fast-fail and alert.
emily: +1 to fast-fail. also add a circuit breaker on per-repo scan retries to avoid duplicate runs for 5m.
oliver: filed GH: https://github.com/redwood-inc/infra-ops/pull/426 — adds `should_retry(err)` with explicit no-retry for KMS AccessDenied and increments job backoff.
sec-bot: Incident created: SEC-2024-2045 — scanner KMS decrypt permission regression. Assigned to @raj, @maria.
raj: working on KMS key policy now. short-term: I'm granting the scanner role kms:Decrypt on the key with condition on srcVpc and role ARN, to match least-privilege. will rotate the role creds after.
maria: while raj fixes perms, we should mute duplicate alerts and add a temporary suppression rule in Snyk/Trivy aggregator so downstream alerts don't flood security team. but suppression must be auditable.
emily: add suppression with tag `kms-decrypt-flap-2024-06-01` and record it in audit log; put TTL 6h and require PR for extension. Also post a timeline in #incidents when done.
oliver: deployed suppression tag to the scan-orchestrator:```\nPATCH /api/v1/suppressions/temporary\n{"tag":"kms-decrypt-flap-2024-06-01","ttl_hours":6,"notes":"temp mute while KMS perms fixed — audit PR #427"}\n```\nraj: perms updated, pushed policy change, redeploying key binding. I'll also add an audit log entry for the policy change and reference the infra PR.
maria: action items for later: 1) triage all duplicated alerts and mark true positives; 2) prioritize patching any vulnerable deps that were missed due to dupes; 3) add unit to pipeline that checks KMS access at startup to fail fast.
emily: for vuln triage: please flag any CVEs with exploit maturity and customer impact. We should bump priority if it's in a public-facing service or in our token handling code.
oliver: created ticket in security-triage board with a checklist and owners. Also opening a small patch PR to bump `github.com/xyz/dependency` from 1.2.3 -> 1.2.5 because one scanner run truncated earlier and missed the upgraded scan.
sec-bot: Audit log recorded: action=apply_suppression actor=oliver metadata=suppressions:kms-decrypt-flap-2024-06-01
raj: redeploy completed, verified decrypt succeeded on a few workers:```\n2024-06-01T09:27:12Z scanner-worker-03 INFO decrypt: success\n2024-06-01T09:27:13Z scanner-worker-03 INFO job queued id=abc\n```\nmaria: great — leaving suppression but lowering TTL to 2h since perms fixed. oliver can you update the suppression TTL?
oliver: done — TTL set to 2h, PR #429 records the change. posted summary to #incidents and pinged on-call. :white_check_mark:
emily: follow-up: let's add an integration test in CI that simulates KMS AccessDenied and ensures we don't retry scans. put it under eng-ml/scan-tests.
oliver: agreed. i'll draft the test. closing thread when triage board is green. thanks all. :thumbsup:
